en.title: Devils regroup after a 9-6 mess as Columbus arrives on a roll
en.deck: New Jersey gave up nine goals in St. Louis on Saturday and has lost two straight after winning 11 of 13. Columbus comes in with two wins in a row, the last one a late comeback in Toronto. Monday opens a home-and-home, and the model has the Devils as clear but smaller favourites than the market.
news: Connor Hellebuyck was pulled 9:03 into Saturday's 9-6 loss after allowing four goals, his first loss since New Jersey acquired him from Winnipeg on Oct. 23. Sheldon Keefe put the blame on the whole team. No starter has been confirmed for Monday.
Devils out: Anthony Mantha (neck surgery), Johnathan Kovacevic and Seamus Casey, all on injured reserve.
Columbus beat Toronto 4-3 with two goals in 52 seconds late in the third: Matthew Knies tied it in his first game back in Toronto since the trade, and Zach Werenski won it.
Sean Monahan is still out for the Blue Jackets. Cam Talbot (7-4-0, .907) has been the steadier of their goalies.
records: Jack Hughes's multi-point game on Saturday was his 134th, tying Kirk Muller for third in Devils history. He leads the team with 29 points.
Werenski has goals in three straight games and points in four.
New Jersey scores 3.78 goals a game, and 16 of its 23 games have gone over 5.5.
Columbus had lost five in a row before this two-game winning streak. The teams meet again in Columbus on Wednesday.

en.title: Kings need goals in Montreal, and the model gives them a real chance

en.title: Stützle and Ullmark carry Ottawa's point streak into a Calgary visit
en.deck: Ottawa has points in eight straight games (6-0-2), tied for its longest run in a decade, and Tim Stützle scored three third-period points to beat the Kings on Saturday. Calgary has won only three of its last nine and may be without Martin Pospisil. The market makes Ottawa a big favourite; the model agrees on the side but not on the size.
news: Pospisil left Saturday's 4-3 overtime loss to Chicago after a high hit from Wyatt Kaiser, who was suspended three games. There was no update on him by Sunday.
Jonathan Huberdeau is on a conditioning stint in the AHL after hip surgery, with five points in two games, and is eligible to return. Kevin Bahl is out long-term.
Ottawa is without Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele. Nick Cousins scored in his return from injury on Saturday.
Neither starting goalie had been confirmed on Sunday.

en.title: Nine straight losses and growing pressure on Hiller as the Leafs visit the Isles
en.deck: Toronto has lost nine in a row (0-8-1), has not won in November and blew a multi-goal lead for the second straight game on Saturday. The Islanders have points in seven straight and Ilya Sorokin is in form. The model and the market agree on the Islanders, almost to the decimal.
news: Fans chanted "Fire Hiller". GM John Chayka publicly backed Jim Hiller, hired in June, on Nov. 17, and no change had been made by Sunday. Auston Matthews called Saturday's loss "inexcusable".
Toronto has the most players on injured reserve in the league. Colton Sissons and Kirill Marchenko practised Sunday in non-contact jerseys, and Jack Roslovic is a game-time decision.
Toronto's starter is open. Sergei Bobrovsky is 3-9-2 with an .874 save percentage, both career worsts, and the Leafs have allowed the most goals in the East.
The Islanders are without Alexander Romanov (knee) for the season. Ondrej Palat scored twice in Saturday's 3-2 win in Detroit.
records: It is Toronto's longest losing streak since an 11-game skid (0-10-1) in early 2015.
Casey Cizikas played his 1,000th NHL game on Saturday, all with the Islanders.
Matthew Schaefer has 85 career points, second all-time among teenage defensemen behind Phil Housley's 132. Simon Holmstrom leads the team with 10 goals and has a career-best seven-game point streak.
Matthews leads Toronto with 33 points and has goals in two straight games. 68% of the Leafs' games have gone over 5.5.

en.title: Kaprizov and the Wild put two club-record streaks on the line in San Jose
en.deck: Minnesota is 11-0-3 in its last 14, tied for the longest point streak in club history, and Kirill Kaprizov has points in every one of those games. Yaroslav Askarov is expected in goal for San Jose, which has had three days off since beating Seattle 4-3.
Macklin Celebrini leads the Sharks in goals (10), assists (19) and points (29). Ivar Stenberg, the No. 2 pick in 2026, has 16 points.

Wallstedt leads the NHL in games (22) and wins (16), with a 1.99 GAA and a .923 save percentage.
San Jose's power play is 5-for-15 over its last four games, but its penalty kill has allowed 15 goals on 35 chances in the last nine.

sv.deck: Minnesota har gått 11-0-3 i de 14 senaste, vilket tangerar klubbens längsta poängsvit, och Kirill Kaprizov har gjort poäng i alla de matcherna. Men Wild saknar Quinn Hughes, och målvaktsfrågan är inte löst. San Jose har 4-1-1 på de sex senaste, och modellen tror mer på Sharks än marknaden gör.
news: Quinn Hughes missar resten av bortaturnén efter en tackling den 19 november. Tränaren John Hynes säger att en hjärnskakning är utesluten. Hughes har 34 poäng på 24 matcher och har mest istid i NHL.
Minnesotas målvakt är oklar: Filip Gustavsson spelade i AHL i lördags, sin första match sedan höftoperationen, och kan göra säsongsdebut. Jesper Wallstedt och Calvin Pickard är de andra alternativen.
Yaroslav Askarov väntas stå för San Jose, som har haft tre vilodagar sedan 4–3-segern mot Seattle.
Macklin Celebrini leder Sharks i mål (10), assist (19) och poäng (29). Ivar Stenberg, tvåa i draften 2026, har 16 poäng.
records: Kaprizovs svit med poäng i 14 raka matcher (28 poäng) tangerar hans eget klubbrekord. Hans 45 poäng är tredje flest i NHL.
Minnesota har tagit poäng i elva raka möten med San Jose (8-0-3) sedan mars 2023, senast 4–1 den 6 november.
Wallstedt leder NHL i matcher (22) och segrar (16), med 1,99 insläppta mål per match och räddningsprocent ,923.
San Jose har gjort 5 mål på 15 powerplay de fyra senaste matcherna, men boxplay har släppt in 15 mål på 35 utvisningar de nio senaste.
betting: Marknaden: Wild 1,47, Sharks 2,75, ungefär 65–35 utan marginal. Modellen har Minnesota på 58 % och ger alltså San Jose klart större chans. Modellen räknar dessutom med Wallstedt, så om Gustavsson startar ändras bilden.
Totalt: över 5,5 ligger på 1,63 (cirka 58 %). Modellen säger 54 %. De tio senaste mötena hade i snitt 7,1 mål, vilket talar för marknaden.
Spelarchanser (modellen): Kaprizov 1+ poäng 77 % (marknaden cirka 74 %), Kaprizov mål 45 % (marknaden cirka 53 % med marginal), Celebrini 1+ poäng 71 % (marknaden cirka 67 %).
